So the same salt yields      the same proxy address on every chain where this factory and `implementation`      share an address, even though each chain can be initialized differently.      `salt` MUST start with the caller's 20-byte address (or be zero in its first      20 bytes); see {SaltDoesNotStartWithCaller}. This matches the create2crunch /      0age ImmutableCreate2Factory salt convention used for offline vanity mining.

This is salt-squatting / front-running protection:         it stops a third party from re-using a salt that was mined (and made         public by deploying on one chain) to occupy the same address on         another chain with attacker-controlled initialization. A salt whose         first 20 bytes are zero is permitted for permissionless deploys.

devdoc.details: A risk council schedules every risk change on the governance core; the CredentialManager's      security council vetoes or fast-tracks it. ## Asset Registry Assets are organized by a uint16 index. Each index represents a **fungible asset class** — not a single token, but all representations of that asset across chains. For example:   - Index 0: USD — USDC on Ethereum, USDC on Solana, USDT on Ethereum, etc.   - Index 1: ETH — WETH on Ethereum, WETH on Arbitrum, etc. Once an index is assigned, it is **permanent**. There is no mechanism to remove or reorder assets; indices are append-only and monotonically increasing. This invariant is critical because external systems (settlement, accounting) depend on index stability. **Important**: There is no on-chain enforcement that all entries under an index are truly fungible with each other. It is the risk council's responsibility to ensure that only fungible representations of the same asset class are registered under a given index. Registering a non-fungible token (e.g. a meme coin) under the USD index would be an operational error with serious consequences.
